profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility in Los Angeles County, CA, per mapping data, with no street address on file. Digital Realty operates named properties in the LA metro, including LAX10 (600 West 7th Street, downtown Los Angeles) and LAX12 (El Segundo), per its own property listings fetched this session, but this session did not confirm which specific building this coordinate corresponds to, so no operator-confirmed address or square footage is reported here rather than guessing.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This mapped point sits within Digital Realty's Los Angeles metro footprint, concentrated in El Segundo near LAX and downtown Los Angeles, a historic hub for submarine cable landing stations and carrier interconnection on the US West Coast. Digital Realty markets its Los Angeles properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Silicon Valley, Northern Virginia, Dallas, Chicago, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage; the company reports its portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than disclosing per-building IT power ratings for any of its facilities, a pattern consistent across every Digital Realty property researched this session, not specific to this building alone.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's LAX10 facility in downtown Los Angeles covers 489,500 square feet across 7 stories with N+1 redundancy for power and cooling. The operator has not published a power capacity figure for this campus, so its actual IT load cannot be determined from the specification. The building holds SOC2, SOC3, PCI-DSS, and ISO 27001 certifications, which qualify it for workloads requiring security and compliance controls across financial services, healthcare, and general enterprise use cases.

LAX10 sits in California, a state where 11 data center facilities have published power capacity online, totaling 365 MW of reported IT load across 103 mapped locations. Without a published power figure, this facility cannot be ranked against peers within the state. The lack of capacity data means LAX10 does not contribute to the known supply picture for AI infrastructure in California, despite its size and location.

The campus offers access to over 25 network providers and seismic resilience for the Los Angeles region. These attributes would support multi-tenant enterprise and financial workloads. Whether LAX10 hosts meaningful AI training or inference capacity depends on its actual power provisioning and the operator's design choices for IT load, neither of which are published on the facility's specification page.
